definition: Capitulate means to surrender and stop resisting.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word capitulate. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know capitulate should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Nine moves from checkmate and an hour behind on the clock, the grandmaster still refused to capitulate.
Wavering is far milder than capitulating — your resolve trembles for a moment, but nothing has been given up yet.
Yielding is weaker than capitulating — you give ground on a point or a moment, while capitulating means the whole resistance ends.

To surrender is to give up, often physically handing yourself or a position over — the white flag moment. Capitulate is the fuller word: not just handing something over but ending the resistance itself, usually after a long fight and on the other side's terms.

To submit is to place yourself under someone else's authority and stop opposing it — it can be quiet, even routine. Capitulate marks a sharper moment: a real fight was fought, the holdout was long, and the surrender is complete and usually on the winner's terms.

Capitulate says more than 'give up' or 'quit' — it means the resistance itself ends, usually after a long fight and usually on the other side's terms.
You quit a hobby; you capitulate to an opponent who has worn you down.
Capitulate is the formal word for the moment resistance ends — sieges, standoffs, long negotiations.
For small everyday moments, 'give in' sounds more natural; reach for capitulate when the fight was real, the holdout was long, and the surrender is complete.
Yield, by contrast, can be partial or temporary — you can yield an inch without capitulating.
